title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #6

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence contains only singular nouns? (1 mark)
   A. Many girls sing.
   B. Girls carry baskets.
   C. The girls carry baskets.
   D. The girl carries a basket.

2. In the passage: Ugali is made from maize flour, what is ugali made from? (1 mark)
   A. millet
   B. maize flour
   C. wheat only
   D. rice

3. Which of these is a cultural food word? (1 mark)
   A. ruler
   B. window
   C. porridge
   D. pencil

4. A good comment during a gallery walk is (1 mark)
   A. You cannot write
   B. This is ugly
   C. Nothing to say
   D. Your spacing is very even

5. Which sentence gives information but not an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Stay indoors.
   B. Today the sky is cloudy.
   C. Bring the clothes.
   D. Close the window.

6. What is reader's theatre? (1 mark)
   A. Reading a script aloud with different parts
   B. A reading test
   C. Acting with costumes only
   D. A drawing lesson

7. A sentence always begins with (1 mark)
   A. a full stop
   B. a comma
   C. a number
   D. a capital letter

8. Which answer is a full sentence for: Why did the pot tip over? (1 mark)
   A. Handle
   B. The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   C. Otieno
   D. Because

9. What is the guessing language game with verbs? (1 mark)
   A. Pupils write verbs on the board silently
   B. Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   C. Pupils read a book
   D. Pupils sing nouns

10. What does listening for comprehension mean? (1 mark)
   A. Listening without thinking
   B. Listening only to music
   C. Listening while sleeping
   D. Listening to understand and remember

11. Which is the best first step to find the meaning of a new word in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Ask nobody
   B. Tear the page
   C. Read the words around it for clues
   D. Skip the whole page

12. How are words arranged in a dictionary? (1 mark)
   A. In alphabetical order
   B. By size of the word
   C. By the number of letters
   D. By colour

13. What should you put after a starting word such as First? (1 mark)
   A. A comma
   B. Nothing
   C. A colon
   D. A question mark

14. What should you keep the same in a paragraph unless there is a reason to change? (1 mark)
   A. The page
   B. The paper colour
   C. The pen
   D. The time of the verbs

15. What is an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing
   B. A written test
   C. A story told aloud
   D. A story kept secret

16. What is a level reader? (1 mark)
   A. A machine
   B. A book written for a particular reading level
   C. A tool for measuring floors
   D. A type of dictionary

17. What does the Kiswahili proverb Kidole kimoja hakivunji chawa teach? (1 mark)
   A. One finger is very strong
   B. Never use your hands
   C. We need to work together
   D. Lice are dangerous

18. What is a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. A group that sells books
   B. A group that meets to share and discuss books
   C. A choir
   D. A team for running

19. Which of these should you include when describing an event? (1 mark)
   A. Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   B. Only the date
   C. Only the name
   D. Nothing

20. What is profit? (1 mark)
   A. Money left after paying the cost
   B. Money spent
   C. A bill
   D. A kind of shop

21. Why do we check a dictionary meaning against the sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Dictionaries are wrong
   B. Words never change
   C. Words can have more than one meaning
   D. Sentences have no meaning

22. Who should you call for a sick animal? (1 mark)
   A. A tailor
   B. A driver
   C. A veterinary doctor
   D. A shopkeeper

23. Which preposition needs two things to make sense? (1 mark)
   A. on
   B. under
   C. between
   D. in

24. Which word means not inside? (1 mark)
   A. between
   B. beside
   C. under
   D. outside

25. What is the meaning of reciting a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Copying it
   B. Writing it
   C. Erasing it
   D. Saying it aloud, usually from memory

26. Which of these is a character? (1 mark)
   A. The last page
   B. A cloudy afternoon
   C. Under the tree
   D. A girl called Neema

27. What is a polite way to disagree in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. You are wrong and silly
   B. I respectfully disagree
   C. Shut up
   D. Leave now

28. Which interjection shows disgust? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck
   B. Hurray
   C. Bravo
   D. Aha

29. Which interjection fits a small mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Wow
   B. Oops
   C. Hurray
   D. Bravo

30. Which interjection shows a request for silence? (1 mark)
   A. Shh
   B. Bravo
   C. Hurray
   D. Aha

31. Which interjection shows praise? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck
   B. Bravo
   C. Oops
   D. Ouch

32. Which line is written correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray Amina: it is Saturday
   B. Amina: Hurray! It is Saturday.
   C. Amina Hurray! It is Saturday
   D. It is Saturday Amina Hurray

33. Which word in a small silver radio is the noun? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. silver
   C. small
   D. radio

34. What is an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. A word that shows action
   B. A word that describes a noun
   C. A joining word
   D. A word that names a person

35. Which sentence uses an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. Computers work.
   B. The heavy computer is on the table.
   C. The computer is on.
   D. On the table.

36. What does answer when they call mean in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. A leader hides
   B. A leader responds when people need them
   C. A leader shouts
   D. A leader sleeps

37. What are images in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Photographs
   B. Diagrams
   C. Maps
   D. Words that make pictures in the mind

38. Why should instruction charts use large clear letters? (1 mark)
   A. To use more ink
   B. So people can read them from a distance
   C. To make them heavy
   D. To hide meaning

39. Which is the correct order for washing hands? (1 mark)
   A. Soap, dry, wet, rinse
   B. Rinse, dry, wet, soap
   C. Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry
   D. Dry, wet, soap, rinse

40. What should the title of an instruction chart do? (1 mark)
   A. Give a joke
   B. Tell what the task is
   C. Be blank
   D. Hide the task

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. List three ways of reading with expression. (3 marks)

42. Complete each sentence with a suitable verb: (a) We ______ our hands before eating. (b) Please ______ the door. (3 marks)

43. Explain why clear instructions are important on a road. (3 marks)

44. Name three questions to ask yourself before telling a personal experience. (3 marks)

45. Give three steps for telling a story fluently. (3 marks)

46. Explain what an oral narrative is. (2 marks)

47. Write the four parts of a telephone conversation and give a short example of one. (4 marks)

48. Explain what an instruction chart is. (2 marks)

49. Write a short telephone conversation of six lines between a pupil and a friend about homework. Use polite expressions. (5 marks)

50. Plan a reader's theatre for a short passage about rain. Say who the roles are, how to practise and how the audience gives feedback. (5 marks)

51. Explain why clear instructions are important when it rains. (3 marks)

52. Give two rules for filling in a form correctly. (2 marks)

53. Compose a short poem of four lines about caring for animals. Make two lines rhyme. (5 marks)

54. Explain how you would perform a choral poem with your class. Include voice, pace and non-verbal cues. (5 marks)

55. Explain what a story setting is. (2 marks)

56. Describe the steps for creating a form for your class about favourite cultural foods. (5 marks)

57. Pick out the nouns in this song line: We roast the maize and boil the beans. (3 marks)

58. Give the plural of each English noun: cabbage, onion. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — The girl carries a basket.
   Girl and basket each name one thing.

2. B — maize flour
   The passage states that ugali is made from maize flour.

3. C — porridge
   Porridge is a food. The others are not.

4. D — Your spacing is very even
   Kind and specific comments help writers.

5. B — Today the sky is cloudy.
   It only tells about the weather.

6. A — Reading a script aloud with different parts
   Pupils read parts with expression.

7. D — a capital letter
   A capital letter shows the start of a sentence.

8. B — The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   A full sentence has a subject and a verb and gives the reason.

9. B — Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   Acting helps everyone connect verbs with actions.

10. D — Listening to understand and remember
   Comprehension is understanding.

11. C — Read the words around it for clues
   Context clues are the words nearby.

12. A — In alphabetical order
   Dictionaries use alphabetical order.

13. A — A comma
   We usually put a comma after First at the start of a sentence.

14. D — The time of the verbs
   Keep past, present or future consistent.

15. C — A story told aloud
   Oral narratives are spoken stories.

16. B — A book written for a particular reading level
   Level readers match the skills of the pupils.

17. C — We need to work together
   One finger cannot crush a louse, so cooperation is needed.

18. B — A group that meets to share and discuss books
   A reading club shares books and reading.

19. A — Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   These details make the event clear.

20. A — Money left after paying the cost
   Profit is gain after costs.

21. C — Words can have more than one meaning
   The right meaning depends on context.

22. C — A veterinary doctor
   Veterinary doctors treat animals.

23. C — between
   Between means with something on each side.

24. D — outside
   Outside means not inside.

25. D — Saying it aloud, usually from memory
   To recite is to say aloud.

26. D — A girl called Neema
   Characters are people or animals.

27. B — I respectfully disagree
   Polite words show respect.

28. A — Yuck
   Yuck shows disgust.

29. B — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

30. A — Shh
   Shh asks for quiet.

31. B — Bravo
   Bravo praises good work.

32. B — Amina: Hurray! It is Saturday.
   It has name, colon and words.

33. D — radio
   Radio names the thing.

34. B — A word that describes a noun
   Adjectives describe nouns.

35. B — The heavy computer is on the table.
   Heavy describes the computer.

36. B — A leader responds when people need them
   It means to respond to people's needs.

37. D — Words that make pictures in the mind
   Images are word pictures.

38. B — So people can read them from a distance
   Clarity helps readers.

39. C — Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry
   This is the logical order.

40. B — Tell what the task is
   The title names the task.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Change loudness, change speed, pause at punctuation, use different voices for characters, use face and hands.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: wash (or clean) and close (or shut)
   Working / marking points: One mark for each suitable verb and one mark for correct spelling.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear road instructions and signs tell drivers and walkers what to do, which prevents accidents and keeps everyone safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for telling what to do, one for preventing accidents, one for safety.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who was there, what happened, where, when, why, how did I feel.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each question.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Know the story well, speak clearly, keep a steady pace, change your voice for characters, look at the audience, end with the lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: An oral narrative is a story told aloud, passed on from person to person, that entertains and teaches.
   Working / marking points: One mark for told aloud and one mark for entertain or teach.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet; say who you are and why you called; talk and listen; say goodbye. Example: Good afternoon, this is Neema speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part and one mark for an example, with 4 marks maximum.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: An instruction chart is a poster that shows the steps of a task in order using short words and often pictures.
   Working / marking points: One mark for steps in order and one for a poster or pictures.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any six lines with greeting, name, reason, polite words, thanks and goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for greeting, one for giving names, one for the reason, one for polite words, one for thanks and goodbye.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Roles such as narrator, farmer, child and rain. Read your part silently three times, mark stressed words, then read aloud with expression. The audience gives one good point and one improvement.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for suitable roles, two marks for practice steps and one mark for feedback.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear instructions tell people what to do to stay safe and dry, so they do not make mistakes or get hurt.
   Working / marking points: One mark for staying safe, one for avoiding mistakes, one for a clear link to rain.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Read instructions first, write neatly inside the spaces, give true information, sign and date it (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on the theme with a pair of rhyming lines, for example Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play, Kind hands keep her safe and well, That is how we care, we tell.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme, two marks for four lines and one mark for a rhyming pair.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Learn the poem well, keep the same pace together, speak clearly with expression, use gestures and smiles as non-verbal cues, look at the audience and practise beforehand.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of five points.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: The setting is the place and time where the story happens.
   Working / marking points: One mark for place and one for time.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Decide the purpose, write a title, list questions such as name, class and favourite food, leave space for answers, write short instructions, test it with a friend and improve it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step up to five.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: maize and beans (and we is a pronoun, not a noun)
   Working / marking points: One mark for maize, one mark for beans, and one mark for not including roast or boil, which are actions.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: cabbages, onions
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.
